findings.title: Prototype-pollution guard can be bypassed through constructor.prototype
findings.impact: The guard only rejects the `__proto__` key. It also tries to detect built-in prototypes by identity comparison. A key path such as `--constructor.prototype.x=1` gets past it. At i=0, `o.constructor` is the `Object` function, so `o` becomes `Object`. At i=1, `o['prototype'] === Object.prototype` is true. The replacement assignment `o[key] = {}` silently fails because `Object.prototype` is non-writable on `Object`. The loop then sets `o = o[key]`, which is still `Object.prototype`. The final assignment `o[x] = value` then pollutes `Object.prototype`. The new tests don't cover this path.
findings.recommendation: Reject `constructor` and `prototype` keys. At minimum, reject `constructor` when it is followed by `prototype`. Alternatively, only traverse own properties, using `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, key)`, and create plain objects for the rest. Add a regression test for `--constructor.prototype.x`.

findings.title: Prototype pollution fix is incomplete: constructor.prototype path bypasses the guards
findings.impact: The patch blocks only the `__proto__` key and tries to detect prototype objects by identity. An attacker who controls argv can pass `--constructor.prototype.polluted=1`. `o['constructor']` is the `Object` function, which is not one of the checked prototypes. On the next iteration `o['prototype'] === Object.prototype`, so the code runs `o[key] = {}`. `Object.prototype` is non-writable, so that assignment silently fails in sloppy mode, and `o = o[key]` still points at the real `Object.prototype`. The final assignment then pollutes it globally. This can cause denial of service, logic or authorization bypass, or code execution gadgets in any application that parses untrusted arguments.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the constructor.prototype pollution vector
findings.impact: The tests only exercise `__proto__` paths, so the bypass above would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add tests for `--constructor.prototype.z=1` and `--x.constructor.prototype.z`. Assert that `{}.z` is undefined. In `setKey`, reject `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` keys, or use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` checks and `Object.create(null)` containers.
